title: Declare SLI surface and degradation orchestration for multiplexed routes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a canonical SLI surface, degradation curves, and orchestration policy for multiplexed routes (routes that can target multiple model variants and region fallbacks). This ticket formalizes how we measure request quality for multiplexed endpoints, map those SLIs to tiered SLOs, and produce deterministic eviction/fallback signals that upstream routing and the autoscaler can act on. Goal: consistent user-visible degradation, clear error-budget accounting per route and per model variant, and predictable cross-region failover behavior.
background: We increasingly route single logical routes to multiple model variants (e.g., fast-quantized vs. high-quality FP16) and across regions. Current SLI measurements assume one model per route, causing noisy error-budget attribution and unexpected evictions when traffic intermingles. Engineering and SRE have observed misattribution of quality regressions and oscillation during bursts when the autoscaler rebalances capacity across variants/regions.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI spec (latency, success, quality) for multiplexed routes is documented and approved by SRE and PM
A degradation curve template (fast/medium/slow) with numeric thresholds for soft/hard eviction is defined
An error-budget escrow primitive that allows borrowing/banking across variants is specified and accepted
A webhook/metric contract for eviction signals is published and consumed by router/autoscaler prototypes
Integration tests that simulate mixed-variant traffic and regional failures pass in CI with deterministic outcomes
out_of_scope: Rewriting existing autoscaler internals (this will be follow-up tasks)
Implementing UI surfaces in Console (separate PM/designer ticket)
Policy changes for Dedicated contract billing

decisions: Use three SLI primitives for multiplexed routes: p95-serving-latency, successful-response-rate (200-range + parseable output), and model-quality-hash-match (0..1 score)
Anchor route SLOs to the weighted aggregate of variant SLIs, with variant weights expressed in route configuration
Introduce an "error-budget-escrow" concept: a short-term credit ledger where underused variants can lend budget to overloaded variants for up to 10 minutes before forced repayment
Eviction signals are tiered: SOFT_EVICT (suggested) and HARD_EVICT (enforce), with soft allowing graceful degraded fallback and hard forcing immediate routing change
Prefer metric-driven thresholds (quantiles) over fixed-percent drop rates to avoid sensitivity to bursty request patterns
tradeoffs: Escrow simplifies short-term variance but adds bookkeeping complexity — chosen because it reduces thrashing in mixed-variant routes
Aggregating quality into a single score loses some model-specific nuance; mitigated by per-variant quality exports and diagnostic labels
Soft evictions may increase tail latency slightly but improve user-visible correctness under transient congestion
implementation_notes: Add per-variant tags to telemetry: variant_id, variant_weight, region, quality_score
Emit a composite route-slack metric used by autoscaler to decide scale actions vs. eviction
Eviction webhook payload: {route, suggested_variant_weights, reason, budget_delta, timestamp, ttl} (schema v1) — router will accept soft/hard signals
Fallback policy: router should prefer nearby region variant with >= 0.8 relative quality unless a HARD_EVICT is present
Prototype code lives in github.com/redwood-inference/router/tree/feature/multiplex-sli (PR linked below)
